Claude not having an image generator is a gap in agentic projects that involve knowledge work. It is quite good at using code to draw or model objects, but image generators from Google and OpenAI give their AIs many more option for doing PowerPoints, mockups, infographics, etc.

Yes, you can make up some of the difference by giving Claude API access but (1) most people will never do this, (2) it means additional expense or difficulty, and (3) the real gain isn't from image generators alone, but from Omni models, and Claude has the least multimodal out.

It is ironic that the thing that is now most annoying about long-running agentic tasks with Large Language Models isn't coding or errors or hallucinations, but the fact that their language gets worse due to drift as a task goes on

Prompt: The instructions are here👇 
Please create a high-end design poster. The overall composition is 3:4 vertical layout, with the top and bottom areas strictly 1:1 in height, each taking up 50% of the screen. 
 
 The upper part retains the main subject, structure, posture, natural light, and color atmosphere of the original photo, with only a slight high-end color grading; it can naturally expand the environment to fit the screen size, but cannot be stretched, distorted, or changed in subject. 
 
 The lower part does not re-edit the photos, but rather uses semantic compression, visual metaphor, and format tower relationships. First, understand the meaning, emotions, symbolism, cultural associations, psychological tension, and deep metaphor of the original image, then extract the most representative relationship, structure, and visual memory points to recreate it. Even if the original image is ordinary, it should extract a memorable and beautiful moment from it.
The lower half of the subject and its necessary environment, relationships, and narrative elements are unified and restructured into a sugar glaze cookie material, forming a complete and consistent miniature landscape, rather than just giving the subject a cookie-like texture. It uses visual language such as bas-relief miniature, iced cookie, fondant, and soft-clay: the contours are rounded and solid, slightly convex, with soft edges and rounded corners, the details are highly summarized, expressing identity characteristics with a small amount of layered icing, embossing, and relief; the surface is matte, delicate, and has fine particles, like small cookie art pieces made with real baking and hand-pounding, avoiding a plastic 3D feel.￼
